description: Plays the channels of a polyphonic cable one at a time, stepping on a clock, with a chance of skipping a step or of adding a random offset to the voltage

params.text: Chooses whether the sequence runs forwards, backwards or jumps to a random channel
Sets the chance that an incoming clock pulse moves the sequence at all, 0 to 1; when it does not, the previous channel keeps playing
Sets the chance that a random offset is added to the voltage on each step, 0 to 1
Sets how far that random offset can reach either side of the channel's own voltage: 0.2V, 0.3V, 0.5V, 0.8V, 1V, 1.2V, 1.3V, 1.5V, 1.8V or 2V
Steps the sequence once, as a rising edge at the clock jack does

inputs.text: The polyphonic cable whose channels are played one at a time; its channel count is the sequence length
A rising edge steps the sequence on by one
A rising edge sends the sequence back to its first channel, or to its last one when it is running backwards

outputs.text: Carries the voltage of the channel the sequence is on, with the random offset added on the steps that take one

notes: a reset is subject to the step probability in the same way a clock pulse is, so a reset that loses the roll changes nothing
the clock jack has no threshold: any voltage away from exactly 0V counts as high
the lamp grid shows one dim lamp per channel of the input and a bright one on the channel being played; the two lamps beside it show a skipped step and an added offset
with nothing patched to the polyphonic input the output is held at 0V

inputs.2: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
